diagnostic_evidence.quote: By definition of $\overline{v}$, there exist $h_m$, $k_m$, $y_m$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs a sequence (t_{k_m},y_m) that (a) converges to (t,x), (b) has v^{h_m}(t_{k_m},y_m)->vbar(t,x), and (c) nearly maximizes v^{h_m}-phi over all of [0,T)xR^d. The definition of vbar only yields sequences realizing the limsup, not (c). The sup is taken over the whole of R^d, but Lemma 4.9 controls v^h only on (-R,R)^d, and no compactness or strict-maximum argument shows that near-maximizers exist in the cube and converge to (t,x). The point y_m-tilde is undefined. Inequality (4.4), c_m->0 and the later use of Lemma 4.9 around y_m all rest on this unproved step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the maximization to a closed ball around x (contained in (-R,R)^d for small h) and use the strict maximum to show that near-maximizers converge to (t,x) and that c_m->0 (standard Barles-Perthame argument). Only the local form of (4.4) is used afterwards.
issues.overall_effect: The subsolution/supersolution property of the half-relaxed limits is not rigorously established as written, so the convergence conclusion of Theorem 4.5 is formally unsupported at this step.
issues.title: Approximate maximizers over all of R^d asserted without compactness/localization argument
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard but nontrivial localization argument that does not change the method or the result.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.9 bounds derivatives of v^h only on (-R,R)^d. Lemma 4.10 needs a uniform (in h) bound on the C^{0,1}(R^d) norm of u = F(t,.;v^h(t,.)), and its proof mollifies and cuts off u on a ball of radius (1+c)R, which extends beyond the cube. Outside the cube v^h is a finite sum of compactly supported kernels with no uniform derivative bound. So the claim that J_m -> 0 does not follow from the cited results as written.

failure_location.quote: imply that $F(t,\cdot;v^h(t,\cdot))$ is bounded and Lipschitz continuous

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the restriction of u to the (convex) cube to R^d by a Lipschitz extension that preserves the sup norm and Lipschitz constant, and apply Lemma 4.10 to the extension. The values of u and I(u) at cube points are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The step J_m -> 0 in the proof of Theorem 4.5 is not justified as stated.
issues.title: Lemma 4.10 applied to a function whose C^{0,1}(R^d) norm is not controlled
issues.why_classification: A short, standard extension argument fixes the step with no loss of rate or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\varphi$ be a $C^3$-function on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: C_1 is the stability bound for v^h from Lemma 4.9 and does not depend on the test function. Lemma 4.11 requires the C^3-norm of phi on O to be <= C_1, and D = {|p|,|gamma| <= C_1} must contain (D phi, D^2 phi) at the point. A viscosity test function is arbitrary, e.g. phi = M(|y|^2+(s-t)^2) touching the zero solution from above with M large, so these hypotheses can fail. Lemma 4.11 is then used outside its hypotheses when applied to phi (the final step of the chain of inequalities).

failure_location.quote: Let $C_1$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:4.9} and fix $\theta\in (0,1/6)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose C_1' = max{C_1, local C^3 bound of phi near (t,x)} in the definition of D and in Lemma 4.11. The proof of Lemma 4.11 works for any value of the constant.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency step comparing with phi in the proof of Theorem 4.5 is not justified for general test functions.
issues.title: Lemma 4.11 applied to arbitrary test function with the fixed stability constant C_1
issues.why_classification: Enlarging the constant is a local routine repair that preserves the method and the conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The growth condition contains the constant 1, but the proof bounds the increment by C*Dt*max sum|D^beta v| only and concludes max|D^alpha v^h(t_k)| <= (1+C Dt) max|D^alpha v^h(t_{k+1})| <= C sup|f|. This is false in general: for F = 1 and f = 0 (which satisfy Assumption 4.1), v^h(t_k) = -(T-t_k) is nonzero while sup|f| = 0. The conclusion C_1 < infinity is still true, but it needs a recursion with an additive term, giving a bound depending on 1+sup|f| and T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Run the discrete Gronwall argument on 1+M_k, i.e. 1+M_k <= (1+C Dt)(1+M_{k+1}), to get M_k <= C(1+sup|f|).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed intermediate bounds in the proof are incorrect. The lemma's statement (existence of C_1) survives.
issues.title: Stability proof drops the constant term of the linear-growth condition
issues.why_classification: A one-line change in the recursion fixes the proof and preserves the lemma and all dependent uses.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses u^eps = tilde u^eps on (-R,R)^d, and also at the collocation points since I depends only on values on Gamma. But zeta(x/R) = 1 is guaranteed only for |x| <= R, while the cube (-R,R)^d contains points with |x| up to sqrt(d) R. For d >= 2 the identity |u^eps - I(u^eps)| = |tilde u^eps - I(tilde u^eps)| can therefore fail at cube points or at points of Gamma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose zeta = 1 on [-1,1]^d (or on {|x| <= sqrt d}) and supported in a slightly larger ball. The remaining estimates change only in constants.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate of Lemma 4.10 is not proved for d >= 2 as written, and the dependent steps (J_m -> 0, terminal condition) inherit this gap.
issues.title: Cut-off function does not equal 1 on the whole cube (d >= 2)
issues.why_classification: A local change of the cut-off preserves the lemma, its rate and the whole argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, take $\delta_1\in (0,1]$ such that $x+\sqrt{\delta}w\in\mathcal{O}$ for all

issues.failure_explanation: The statement asserts one delta_1 (and C) valid for all x in the open set O and all phi defined only on O. The proof fixes x and chooses delta_1 so that x + sqrt(delta) w stays in O for all |w| <= delta^{-theta}. For x near the boundary of O no uniform delta_1 exists, and phi is undefined at the points used in the Taylor expansion. The proof therefore gives only an x-dependent threshold (uniform on compact subsets of O).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the lemma for x in a compact subset of O (or for phi defined on a larger neighbourhood), with delta_1 depending on that subset.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is stated more strongly than proved. The application, with y_m converging to an interior point, needs only the compact-subset version.
issues.title: Lemma 4.11 claims a delta_1 uniform in x in O, but the proof's delta_1 depends on x
issues.why_classification: Restricting the quantifier to the region actually used is a local statement fix with no loss for the main argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we have confirmed the condition on the interpolation matrix

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 4.3(ii) is an asymptotic condition on a family indexed by h -> 0 (N -> infinity, R -> infinity) with constants independent of h. Section 5 only inspects finitely many N (N <= 500 for d=1, N <= 10^4 for d=2) and itself says the assumption 'seems' to hold. The Conclusion nevertheless says the condition has been 'confirmed' and 'can be checked by countable procedures'. No finite computation can verify it, and the paper proves it for no kernel/point-set family. The convergence theorem therefore remains conditional on an unverified hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: which can be checked by countable procedures

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to say the decay condition is verified numerically only for the tested N and is assumed (not proved) in general.
issues.overall_effect: The Conclusion overstates how far the hypothesis of Theorem 4.5 has been validated. The theorem is a conditional result.
issues.title: Conclusion overstates what the numerics establish about the decay assumption
issues.why_classification: Only the wording of the scope claim needs correcting; no theorem or proof changes.
